scenes.name: a pensioners' paradise
scenes.narration: In 1985, Bangalore was a quiet city of gardens and retirees. People called it a pensioners' paradise.

scenes.note: 1985 — Miller's Road. Texas Instruments opens India's first multinational R&D centre.
scenes.narration: Then Texas Instruments opened India's first multinational research centre, on Miller's Road.
To talk to America, it needed a satellite dish. The dish arrived on a ==bullock cart.==

scenes.title: How a quiet city changed

events.label: Texas Instruments opens India's first multinational R&D centre

scenes.narration: Infosys had already moved here in 1983. Forty years later, the city's tech workforce crossed one million.
Tech parks rose across Whitefield, Electronic City and Manyata, glass towers where the fields used to be.

scenes.label: tech workers in [[Bengaluru]]
scenes.narration: Over one million tech workers. One of the largest tech talent pools in Asia.
Today, Karnataka produces forty one percent of India's software exports, and nearly all of it comes from Bengaluru.

scenes.title: Written in Bengaluru. Used everywhere.
scenes.source: RBI: US & Canada are the top destination for India's software exports
scenes.narration: Most of that software flows to America and Europe, into the apps and banks people use every day.
From a bullock cart, to the city that codes the world.

scenes.headline: Bengaluru.
scenes.narration: Bengaluru. Follow for the next story.
